skill.name: github-pr-best-practices
skill.description: Best practices for creating GitHub pull requests with conventional commit titles, structured descriptions, test plans, GitHub CLI guidance, and English or Japanese output.
skill.summary: Create structured GitHub pull requests with conventional titles, useful summaries, and clear test plans.
skill.author: 1natsu172

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, documentation links, and checklist text. No evidence found for prompt injection, credential exfiltration, malware behavior, or covert network activity in SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md, or resources/pr-template-examples.md.

remediation.issue: CLI examples can create or update remote GitHub pull requests when executed.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit note that GitHub CLI commands require user confirmation, authentication, and the intended repository context.

remediation.issue: Some examples use shell command substitution for multi-line PR bodies.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer body files or clearly quoted heredocs to reduce shell quoting mistakes in copied commands.

remediation.issue: Markdown inline code and fenced commands create noisy static-analysis signals.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples hardcoded and avoid interpolating user-controlled shell fragments in future revisions.

static_findings.snippet: - `style`: Code style changes (formatting, no logic change)
- Component name: `fix(button): resolve click handler issue`
- Area of code: `docs(api): update endpoint documentation`
Use English when no language is specified or when language is `en`:
If the project has a PR template at `.github/pull_request_template.md`:
2. Start with `--draft` flag for work in progress
3. Use `cat <<'EOF'` (with quotes) to prevent variable expansion
4. `gh pr create` automatically pushes the branch (no manual push needed)
- ❌ `git push -u origin branch && gh pr create`
- `git-analysis`: Use to gather commit and branch information
- Avoid implementation details (those are in the code)

content.value_statement: Pull requests often lose context when titles, summaries, and tests are inconsistent. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to produce structured GitHub PR content.
actual_capabilities: Formats PR titles with Conventional Commits types and optional scopes.
Builds PR summaries and test plans with concise checklist items.
Supports English and Japanese pull request descriptions.
Follows existing project pull request templates without changing section order.
Provides GitHub CLI examples for draft, ready, review, comment, and merge workflows.
Guides commit analysis from merge base so the full branch is represented.
limitations: It does not inspect repository history unless paired with git tooling.
It does not run tests, verify CI status, or prove the PR is correct.
Language examples focus on English and Japanese only.
GitHub CLI actions require authentication and explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Draft a Feature PR
use_cases.description: Create a conventional title, short summary, and practical test plan for a new feature branch.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Apply consistent sections, checklists, and Conventional Commits titles across many repositories.

use_cases.title: Prepare Bilingual PR Notes
use_cases.description: Generate clear English or Japanese PR descriptions while keeping the same structure and review expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple PR Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a small change with known context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a draft GitHub PR description for this change: [describe change]. Use English, a Conventional Commits title, a summary, and a test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Turn Commits Into PR Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when commit messages describe the branch work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review all commits on this branch from the merge base. Propose a PR title, summary bullets, and test plan that cover the full branch.

prompt_templates.title: Follow a Project Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the repository has a pull request template.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the repository pull request template exactly. Fill each section for this change, keep section order, and mark non-applicable sections as N/A.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Complex Bilingual PR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for larger or cross-functional work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Japanese PR description for this multi-commit change. Include background, implementation details, migration notes if needed, and a specific test plan.

output_examples.input: Create a draft PR for adding OAuth2 login support.
output_examples.output: Title: feat(auth): add OAuth2 login. The description summarizes authentication, token refresh, and error handling. The test plan covers login, refresh, and failure cases.

output_examples.input: Write a PR for a refactor with no functional changes.
output_examples.output: Title: refactor(auth): improve module structure. The description states no behavior changed and asks reviewers to verify existing tests and login flows.

output_examples.input: Generate Japanese PR notes for a performance improvement.
output_examples.output: The output uses Japanese section headings for summary and test plan, with bullets covering query caching, benchmarks, invalidation, and regression checks.

best_practices: Analyze the full branch before writing the title or summary.
Keep summaries focused on what changed and why it matters.
Use specific test plan items that reviewers can verify.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague summaries such as updated stuff or fixed things.
Do not change a repository pull request template without a clear request.
Do not create or update remote PRs without user confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill create pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance and command examples. Actual GitHub CLI actions still require tool access, authentication, and user approval.

faq.question: Can it use an existing pull request template?
faq.answer: Yes. It instructs the assistant to preserve template sections, order, and required fields.

faq.question: Which languages are supported?
faq.answer: The skill includes explicit guidance for English and Japanese PR descriptions.

faq.question: Does it enforce Conventional Commits?
faq.answer: It guides titles toward Conventional Commits types, scopes, and imperative descriptions.

faq.question: Can it verify that tests pass?
faq.answer: No. It can write a test plan, but it does not run tests or validate CI by itself.

faq.question: Is it useful without GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use the generated title and description in the GitHub web interface.
